newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's Abiola in good health in detention.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's Abiola in good health in detention.

text.p: Moshood Abiola, presumed winner of Nigeria's annulled presidential election, is in good health and his living conditions have improved nearly three years after he was detained, his doctor has said.
Abiola, one of Nigeria's richest men, has been held in a secret location since June 23, 1994, after he proclaimed himself president in defiance of military ruler General Sani Abacha.

"I met him alive, very well and in high spirits, the level of which I have not seen him in the last two years," Ore Falomo, Abiola's personal physician, told the opposition Tell magazine in a report published on Monday.
The military government allowed Falomo to meet Abiola in the Nigerian capital Abuja on May 10 and the doctor told the magazine they spent 90 minutes together, their first meeting in 14 months.
Abiola is widely believed to have won a June 1993 election meant to restore democracy but annulled by then military president General Ibrahim Babangida.
Falomo, a personal friend, appeared to have been allowed to see the politician following a rumour that he was dead.
He said Abiola was now held in more decent circumstances.
"The house is well furnished...It's a nice building with a good compound, a bungalow," Falomo said.
He said that despite his long detention, Abiola's spirit had not been broken.
Abiola was charged with treason shortly after his arrest but last appeared in court in August 1994. The case has since been stalled by legal technicalities.

International and local pressure on Abacha to free Abiola has yielded no results. The Nigerian ruler is pursuing a programme he says will lead to his handover of power to an elected president in October next year.
